summary: A 1934 L-4 cab on a log crib on Oreana Ridge; used for summer fire watch and fire support into the 1950s, survived the 2011 Saddle Complex fire, and open to public use.

facts.design: L-4 cab with catwalk on a log crib base, two stories overall

staffing.status: last used in the 1960s; no current staffing reported

access.note: Open to public use per firelookout.com; Idaho Fire Lookouts lists it as Drive-Up FCFS; reached by a gravel 4x4 track

visit.trail_note: Gravel 4x4 track FR-067 from Spring Creek Road, about 2.8 miles; high clearance and 4WD advised (third-party guide)

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Salmon-Challis National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR describes the log crib as one story; firelookout.com calls the structure 2-story and a local history describes a cab atop a log first floor. Read together, the lookout is two stories overall (cab on a one-story crib).
firelookout.com and the 1955 newspaper item use the older name Salmon National Forest; NHLR and the current forest name is Salmon-Challis National Forest. Same forest.

notes_for_editor: Staffing evidence is sparse: the last documented staff is 1956 (Clary) and the 1969 item is a plan, not a confirmed abandonment. The 1939 item names 'a forest lookout near Horse Creek' without naming Oreana; the story says so. Climbability of the cab is not stated in any source read, so no climbable flag is recorded. Brief's access 'unknown' is now public (firelookout.com 'open to public use'). The 2011 NHLR registration date is now confirmed on the NHLR page (Date Registered September 24, 2011); an earlier note said it was not visible. Road description comes from a third-party driving guide (Dangerous Roads), not the Forest Service; check current FR-067 conditions before publishing. Dangerous Roads gives 8,103 ft for the ridge peak; firelookout.com and NHLR give 8,075 ft for the lookout. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives the 1934 cab's garage as log; the 1960s 'last used for emergency services' is decade-only.
